identity.title: Star Formation and the Interstellar Medium in z > 6 UV-luminous Lyman-break Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) detections of atomic carbon line and dust continuum emission in two UV-luminous galaxies at redshift 6.

question.value: What are the [C II] and FIR dust properties (SFR, [CII]/FIR ratio, dynamics) of two UV-luminous z>6 LBGs, and what do systemic redshifts from [C II] imply for Lyα velocity shifts at z~6?

evidence.quote: Using the interstellar atomic carbon line to derive the systemic redshifts we investigate the velocity of Ly$\alpha$ emission emerging from high-$z$ galaxies.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00815.S.
A total bandwidth of 7.2 GHz was employed in Band 6 using 4 dual-polarization sub-bands between 249 and 272 GHz.
One of the sub-bands was centered at the \[C ii\] line (rest frame 1900.5369 GHz) for each source.
Observations were made during ALMA cycle 2, in June 2014, with between 29 and 32 antennas, and a maximum baseline of 650m.
For both sources, the Gaussian restoring beam was close to circular, with a FWHM = 0.50".
A total of 95 minutes on-source integration time was obtained for each galaxy.
Observations were made during ALMA cycle 2, in June 2014
Images from Data Release 3 in bands $Z, Y, J, H$ and $Ks$ were obtained
Both $z>6$ galaxies are clearly detected at both 3.6 and 4.5$\mu$m
The spectrum of CLM 1 was obtained using FORS2 at the ESO VLT with a spectral resolution of $R=1400$

claims.hypothesis: Do UV-luminous z~6 LBGs have low FIR luminosity and high [CII]/FIR?
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 6 [CII] and 1.2 mm continuum of two LBGs
claims.result: [CII]/FIR ~5e-3 to 1e-2, FIR low relative to SFR
claims.finding: [CII] should be readily detectable in the reionization epoch

evidence.quote: The \[C ii\] to FIR ratios are found to be higher than at low redshift

claims.hypothesis: Do Lyα velocity shifts decrease at high z?
claims.experiment: Lyα offsets relative to [CII] systemic redshift compared with lower-z sample
claims.result: +430 km/s for CLM 1; +265 or +504 km/s for WMH 5

evidence.quote: Our analysis shows no observational evidence for velocity shifts that decrease as a function of redshift, at a given Ly$\alpha$ equivalent width.

why_this_data.value: Targets chosen because UV luminosity, stellar mass and redshift comparable to Himiko

evidence.quote: CLM 1 and WMH 5 were selected for study because their UV luminosity, stellar mass and redshift are comparable to the galaxy *Himiko*

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: No CMB correction applied since the effects are comparable and opposite

evidence.quote: the two effects are of comparable size and opposite sign for likely dust temperatures at this redshift, so we make no correction.

limitations_admitted.value: Single continuum point; dust temperature unconstrained

evidence.quote: Since we only have one continuum point and no constraints on dust temperature, we cannot make an accurate correction
